submitted_request.prompt:
One continuous six-second photorealistic cinematic OVERHEAD shot of a Diwali paper ground chakri spinning and burning out. CAMERA: locked directly above, looking vertically DOWN at exactly 90 degrees to the floor. A true flat top view for the ENTIRE shot, absolutely no oblique/three-quarter/side view, no camera movement, no tilting, no cuts.
Use @image_1 ONLY for the object's visual design: a flat round cardboard-and-paper chakri, vivid red outer top, bright cyan/blue zigzag circular band, yellow concentric inner ring, pale cream centre; beneath the paper top is a thick spiral coil of paper-wrapped tube with red, blue and off-white stripes. It is lightweight paper with a slightly laminated cardboard cover and visible paper folds, never brass or steel. Omit ALL reference watermarks and writing. One chakri only, isolated on an empty matte deep blue-charcoal #080E16 floor. Subtle blue #2F81F7 ambient fill. The complete object occupies the central THIRD of the landscape frame, with dark empty space around it for sparks. No hands, people, packaging, logos or other objects.
TIMELINE: 0-0.8 seconds, the colourful round paper disk rests flat in exact top view, with its striped outer coiled paper tube clearly visible as a ring. A small fuse at the outer end glows and hisses. 0.8-4.5 seconds, the entire wheel accelerates into a rapid clockwise horizontal ground spin around its centre vertical axis, throwing long fine warm-gold curved sparks tangentially across the floor. The red/blue/yellow top develops natural circular rotational motion blur. IMPORTANT CONSUMPTION: the burning point travels along the red-blue-white paper-wrapped coiled tube. The striped coil is visibly and progressively USED UP from the outer end inward while spinning: the spent outer sections scorch, turn to fine ash and disappear; the remaining striped coil steadily recedes and thins. Show the amount of striped paper tube diminishing continuously, ending nearly completely spent. Never leave a fresh unchanged striped outer rim after the burn. The paper cover subtly singes at its perimeter. 4.5-6 seconds, the final tube sections finish burning, the rotation slows and stops, sparks diminish into a few golden embers, leaving only the spent/singed thin cardboard disk and tiny ash on the dark floor. The spent coil must not magically reappear. Keep a clean final dark frame suitable for a transition to a Diwali greeting, which will be composited later.
PHYSICS: wheel stays flat on the ground; it does not tip, float, levitate, turn into a diya or deform like molten plastic. Sparks have delicate heads and trails, realistic falloff, natural motion blur and a soft floor reflection. Exposure stays controlled, no blown-out white screen. A polished festive commercial, with clear progressive paper-coil consumption as the main visual detail.
AUDIO: synchronized fuse hiss, rising airy spinning whirr, many bright fine granular firework crackles, then soft decay as it burns out. Natural comfortable level; no music, speech, chanting, cheering, narration or huge bang.
NO text, typography, captions, logos, brand names, stock-photo watermark, computer UI, metallic spinner, mechanical gear, plastic toy, purple/magenta background, aerial rocket, sky explosion, neon portal, strobing, camera shake, camera tilt, extra objects or new paper tube appearing. The Happy Diwali typography and aerial fireworks will be added AFTER this opening shot, so do not generate them here.
